libx.lookup_running: Already looking up artists. Results show up when it finishes.

libx.intro: A library check reads your music folders and the songs' tags. Everything below adds more, and each is off until you switch it on: some take a lot of this computer's time, some ask services online.
libx.sound_analysis_note: Listens to every song once, on this computer, for "more like this", similar artists, radio by sound, smart play, and even volume for songs without ReplayGain tags. It's the heaviest job here: on a modest computer about a song a second, using up to half the processor, so a big library takes hours the first time.
libx.heavy_note: For sound analysis and AI listening. They pause between songs, so music never waits for them.
libx.when_idle: Only while no music is playing
libx.artist_info_note: Sends artist names to Deezer, Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons, after each library check that finds new artists. Pictures in your own folders always win.
libx.more_pictures: More pictures, as a slideshow on artist pages and on the TV page while their songs play
libx.more_pictures_note: (from the sources you choose below, with credits. Commons and fanart.tv use MusicBrainz to find the right artist. Each artist's pictures are fetched the first time they're shown.)
libx.picture_limits_note: These apply to extra artist pictures. Downloaded images are resized before they enter the cache. The cache limit also covers album art and thumbnails; existing files stay when you lower it.
libx.cache_max: Art cache maximum MB (0 = no cap)
libx.sources_note: Choose automatic sources here. MusicBrainz identifies artists and albums when enabled above. Source changes are applied as each artist is checked again.
libx.src_deezer: Deezer (main artist portrait, local copy, no key)
libx.allow_remote: Allow remote image display (visitors load images from the provider)
libx.src_unsplash: Unsplash (browse and select, remote display only)
libx.browse_note: Open these libraries to find artist photos. For licensed images, use Manage pictures on an artist page to upload a copy you are allowed to use, with its credit.
libx.musicbrainz_note: Album covers, album and artist genres, and exact artist matches (better photos and bios), from MusicBrainz and the Cover Art Archive. Sends artist and album names. MusicBrainz needs no account, but asks apps to say who to contact if something goes wrong; it's sent with each request.
libx.looking_now: Looking up artists... New pictures show up when it's done.
libx.identify_note: Needs an AcoustID key and the MusicBrainz contact above. Song fingerprints (not the audio) go to AcoustID. It only runs when you start it, below.
libx.acoustid_before: Free for non-commercial use: register an application at
libx.spotify_note: Lets the library editor's album layout look albums up on Spotify (track lists and covers), next to MusicBrainz, Deezer and Apple. DJINN only contacts Spotify when you search there, sending what you typed and the app's keys.
libx.secret_saved: Saved. Paste a new one to replace it
libx.secret_hint: View client secret, then paste it
libx.spotify_how_1: choose Create app: any name (DJINN) and description; Redirect URI
libx.spotify_how_2: (Spotify asks for one, DJINN doesn't use it); tick Web API; save. Then open the app's Settings, copy the Client ID, choose View client secret and copy that. Saving checks them with Spotify.
libx.youtube_note: Lets anyone on this server import a YouTube or YouTube Music playlist from its link, here, on GO and in the Android app. Without a key, DJINN never contacts YouTube. With one, it sends only the key and the playlist's id when someone imports a link, nothing about who's asking. YouTube still sees this server's internet address.
libx.key_saved: Saved. Paste a new key to replace it
libx.youtube_how_after: create a project, enable YouTube Data API v3, and create an API key.

lyrp.title: Lyrics
lyrp.intro: DJINN reads lyrics from a .lrc file beside each song (same name) and from the songs' own tags, and keeps them in its database. Timed lyrics follow the music on the Playing tab, in GO and on the lyrics page; any lyrics can be searched by typing a line you remember.
lyrp.lookup: Look up missing lyrics on LRCLIB
lyrp.lookup_note: A free, open lyrics site (lrclib.net). Each song's artist, title, album and length are sent, one song at a time.
lyrp.ai_note: Show a note on lyrics an AI worked on
lyrp.ai_note_note: A line under the lyrics saying an AI made the words, or timed them. On by default.
lyrp.page_note: Full-screen lyrics for a TV or spare screen, without signing in, at

lyrp.blocked.one: {n} song has lyrics you removed as bad, which won't be taken from the same source again unless its text changes.
lyrp.blocked.other: {n} songs have lyrics you removed as bad, which won't be taken from the same source again unless its text changes.

lyrp.recheck_note: Recheck reads every song again (for .lrc files added since) and asks LRCLIB again. Export downloads a zip of .lrc files laid out like your music folders and named like the songs, so unzipping it over a music folder puts each one beside its song.
lyrp.import_note: A zip of .lrc or .txt files laid out like your music folders (the same layout as the export above). Each file is matched to a song by the artist and title in its [ar:] and [ti:] lines, or by its place in the zip when those are missing. It only fills songs that have no lyrics: lyrics from song files, tags and LRCLIB always win. Files that look like code or markup are thrown out and listed. Up to 250 MB and 150,000 files per zip; send several zips for a bigger library.
lyrp.replace: Replace lyrics from an earlier import
lyrp.replace_other: Let better imported lyrics replace lyrics from files, tags and LRCLIB
lyrp.better_note: "Better" means timed over plain, or a person's words timed by an AI over plain words. Lyrics an AI made by listening never replace anyone's, and nothing replaces a person's timed lyrics with equal or worse ones.
lyrp.unasked: Import even if LRCLIB has not been asked about the song yet
lyrp.unasked_note: Unless this is ticked, songs LRCLIB hasn't been asked about are skipped (and counted), so it gets the first go.

lyrp.because.one: because it looked like code or markup, not lyrics:
lyrp.because.other: because they looked like code or markup, not lyrics:

ident.intro: Finds the album, year, and genres for songs whose tags are missing them, by their sound (AcoustID and MusicBrainz). You choose what to use; DJINN keeps it in its own database and your files aren't changed.
ident.need_key: Add an AcoustID key above first.
ident.need_contact: Add a MusicBrainz contact above first.

gg.title: Genre Containers
gg.intro: Group similar genres into containers, so "black metal", "death metal" and "speed metal" all show as "Metal". While this is on, genre lists, the genre cloud and genre pages show the containers instead of the genres in them, and a container's page has every song of its genres. Artist, album and song pages still show the real genres, with the container first in pink. Your music files and the genres DJINN knows aren't changed; turn this off to put everything back.
gg.working: Working out how the genres relate...
gg.not_enough: Not enough related genres to group yet. Genres relate when songs share them or sound alike, so this works better after a library check and sound analysis.
gg.how: Genres are grouped by how related they are: songs they share, and how alike their songs sound. Slide left for fewer, broader containers, right for more, closer ones. Genres you placed by hand and containers you made or changed are left as they are.
gg.moving: Moving {genre}: choose Move here on a container.
gg.none: No containers yet. Use Auto-group, or make one and drag genres into it.
xf.title: Crossfade
xf.note: Songs from the same album always join without a gap, so live albums and DJ mixes flow as recorded.
rg.off_note: Songs play as loud as they were made.
rg.track_note: Best for parties and shuffled playlists.
rg.album_note: Quiet and loud songs on an album keep their difference. Good for playing whole albums.
rg.title: Volume Leveling (ReplayGain)
rg.intro: Keeps songs at an even loudness, so a quiet old track isn't followed by a blast. Uses ReplayGain tags when a file has them. For files without, DJINN measures each song once and keeps the result in its own database; your files aren't changed. Applies from the next song.
rg.boost_note: Leveled songs play quieter than most modern masters. Raise this if everything sounds too soft; songs never get pushed into clipping.
rg.analysis_off: Songs without ReplayGain tags are measured by sound analysis, which is off, so they play unchanged. Switch it on under
rg.not_yet: Songs not measured yet play unchanged.
eq.party_note: Shape the party mix on every output, including casting and Tune In. Normal levels stay intact; peaks near clipping are softened.
out.remove_q: Stop playing through {name} and remove it?
out.clock_note: Others keep time with this one
out.title: Outputs
out.intro: Play through more than one device at once, like the stereo and a Bluetooth speaker in the next room. DJINN keeps them in time. Bluetooth lags a few hundred milliseconds behind wired outputs, so raise the delay on the wired ones until everything lines up.
out.default: The system default right now, which already plays through "System default"
out.none: No other devices found. Connect a Bluetooth speaker or plug something in, then try again.
out.bt_note: Bluetooth speakers show up here once they're paired and connected to this computer.
cast.new_link_q: Give the live stream a new address? Anyone listening with the old one stops, and casts restart.
cast.new_link_done: The stream has a new address
cast.showing: Showing the TV page with sound
cast.title: Cast to TVs and Speakers
cast.intro: Play the party on Chromecasts, Google TVs, Nest speakers, smart TVs (DLNA), and Sonos, several at once. "Show on TV" puts the TV page on the screen, with what's playing, what's next, and the join code, and plays the music too. Network devices run a few seconds behind this computer's speakers and can't be synced to them, so use either casts or local speakers in a room, not both. Speaker groups from the Google Home app stay in sync with each other.
cast.volume_tv: Volume is set on the TV.
cast.none: No devices found. They need to be on the same Wi-Fi as this computer, and switched on.
sp.clear_q: Forget what {name} parties liked? The request log keeps its history.
sp.title: Smart Play
sp.intro: When nobody has requested anything, DJINN picks songs itself. Smart Play has it learn from the party: songs people request come up more, and so do others by the same artists and in the same genres. Songs people skip come up less.
sp.learn: Learn from the party for wild play and radio
sp.playlists: Also use it for shuffled playlists (every song still plays once before any repeats)
sp.mood_note: Everyone at the party gets a dial on the Playing tab, from chill to hype. The auto mix then favors songs whose energy fits what the room wants: faster, punchier songs for hype, calmer ones for chill. Each person's setting counts for 40 minutes. It works for wild play, radio and shuffled playlists, using sound analysis (Admin > Library), so songs not analyzed yet aren't moved either way.
sp.styles_note: Each style keeps its own memory, so a Halloween party doesn't change what plays at the family BBQ. Use the one that fits tonight: requests, songs played through, and skips count toward it.
sp.nothing: Nothing yet. It learns as people request and skip songs while this style is in use.
sp.number_note: The number is how much more (or less) often it comes up. Artists and genres count for less than a song itself.
sch.mood_middle: Leave the dial in the middle
sch.title: Party Schedule
sch.intro: Time rules for the evening, like a quiet playlist until 9, then wild play turned up. As each rule starts, DJINN sets what it says once; anything changed by hand afterwards stays until the next rule. A rule that ends earlier than it starts runs past midnight. Times are this computer's.

lf.title: Library Folders
lf.intro_3: . In a read only folder you can see everything (the editor, the compare and the Problems page read every folder), but nothing changes, so use it for a folder someone else looks after. In a read and write folder the editor changes the files themselves, in place: tags, covers, names and places, copying in and deleting. Every change is in the editor's history and can be undone. Making a folder read and write checks that DJINN can write there.

rm.title: Rooms
rm.intro: Each room is its own party: its own queue, playlist, volume and skip votes, played on the speakers and nodes you put in it. A room uses Main's queue rules (Admin > Rules) until you give it its own. Drag an endpoint from one room to another to move it; click one to open its settings. People pick their room in the app, or scan a room's join code to walk straight in. Your song likes and what the party learns are shared across the house.

gp.forwarding_note_2: , and other Subsonic apps need to be told to accept it.
gp.plain: Also allow unencrypted connections from outside

gp.https_note: Give GO a public DNS name and run an HTTPS reverse proxy on this computer. With Caddy, add this site to its Caddyfile:

cv.intro: Off unless you turn it on. Then DJINN makes MP3 copies for devices that can't play a song's format, for people who turn on "Save data" in GO, and for phone apps asking for a lower quality. Each song is converted once and kept, so it uses this computer's processor the first time only. Roles choose who can use it (under Users).

vp.intro: What a node's screen draws while it shows the visualizer (Admin > Nodes > Screen). Each node measures its own speaker and draws it in step. These are for every node, unless a node has its own.

visual.about_mirror: Bars growing up and down from the middle.
visual.about_wave: The sound wave itself, across the screen.
visual.about_spectrogram: The song drawn as it plays: time across, pitch up, loudness as color.
visual.about_scope: Left against right: a line for mono, a cloud for wide stereo.
visual.about_mountain: The spectrum as a lit range of hills with its reflection.
visual.about_vu: Two needle meters, left and right, like an old amplifier.
visual.about_circle: The wave wrapped around a ring that swells with the bass.
visual.about_particles: Sparks thrown out from the middle, a burst on every beat.
visual.about_terrain: A checkerboard of glowing pillars: bass in the middle, treble at the edges, rolling into the distance.
visual.about_flyover: A checkerboard of pillars seen from a helicopter circling slowly; the middle bounces with the bass, further out with higher sounds.
visual.about_warp: Swirling trails, each frame fed into the next.
visual.about_tunnel: Flying down a tunnel that rings with the music.
visual.about_plasma: Flowing color that bends with bass and mids.
visual.about_kaleidoscope: Eight mirrored slices of moving patterns.
visual.about_nebula: Slow clouds of colored gas that glow with the bass.
visual.about_stars: Flying through stars, faster with the bass.

pa.intro: Anything that changes your music library (the folders and the files in them) sits behind this lock: writing tags, renaming, moving, adding songs. Opening such an area asks for your password, and at Max a code from your authenticator app too. It locks again when you leave Admin, or after ten minutes without use. DJINN's own database (tag corrections kept in DJINN, history, lyrics) is not behind it.
pa.recovery: The host's recovery command was used on {when} for "{name}". If that wasn't you or another admin, treat the computer as compromised.
pa.lock_off: The lock is off: protected actions are open to every admin.
pa.max_needs: Max needs two-step sign-in on your account. Set it up on your Account page first.
pa.off_warning: With the lock off, anyone who can sign in as an admin can change or delete your files and really mess things up for you. That includes someone at an unlocked computer, a stolen session or a guessed password.
pa.type_off: Type OFF to turn the lock off
pa.audit_note: A record of each unlock, failed try, change of level and library change made through a protected area: who, when, and from where. You can turn it off and delete it. Turning it off or deleting records needs the area unlocked, and while the trail is on, a purge leaves one record of itself. Turn it off first for no trace.
